chief_complaint: excruciating pain with bowel movements and bright red blood on toilet paper
hpi_details: 30M presents with severe, tearing, glass-like pain during bowel movements, lasting for hours afterwards. He also notices a few drops of bright red blood on the toilet paper. He suffers from chronic constipation.
concerns: terrified to go to the bathroom due to pain
expectations: wants a cream to numb the pain

core_concepts: Pain during and after defecation is the hallmark, often with minor bleeding.
common_misconceptions: Misdiagnosing as purely hemorrhoids without inspecting for a fissure.
dangerous_errors: Performing a digital rectal exam when an acute fissure is obvious on visual inspection (causes extreme unnecessary pain).
management_principles: Stool softeners, sitz baths, topical vasodilators (nifedipine/nitroglycerin).
boundaries_and_exceptions: Lateral fissures should raise suspicion for Crohn's, HIV, or syphilis.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 30M with extreme pain during defecation and minor bright red blood per rectum.
reference_soap.objective: Visual inspection of the anus reveals a posterior midline mucosal tear. DRE deferred due to severe pain.
reference_soap.plan: Topical nifedipine ointment, docusate sodium, high-fiber diet, sitz baths.

learning_objectives: Recognize the clinical presentation of an anal fissure vs hemorrhoids.

teaching.one_liner: Severe, sharp pain during defecation with small amounts of bright red blood, highly characteristic of an anal fissure.

must_ask.say: Does the pain happen during or right after a bowel movement, and how long does it last?
Have you noticed blood — is it bright red and only on the toilet paper or in the bowl?
Do you tend to have hard stools or constipation?
Have you had this kind of pain with bowel movements before?
Have you noticed any swelling, pus, or fever around your bottom?

history.answer: Doctor, it feels like I am passing broken glass every time I have a bowel movement, and I see bright red blood on the toilet paper.
The blood is bright red, just like fresh blood from a small paper cut.
It is just a few drops on the toilet paper when I wipe, not mixed inside the stool itself.
It started three days ago after passing an unusually hard stool, and it happens every time I go.
The pain is excruciating and tearing, like razor blades cutting into me while passing stool.
A severe, burning throb lingers for several hours after I finish using the bathroom.
No, I haven't felt any protruding lumps, and there is no itching around my anus.
Yes, I have had chronic constipation for years and frequently have to strain hard to pass dry, lumpy stools.
No, my stools are firm and bulky, not pencil-thin or narrowed.
No, once the stool passes, I feel like my rectum is empty.
No, my stomach does not hurt at all and I have no cramping.
No, I have not had any loose stools, diarrhea, or slimy mucus.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, there is no swollen painful boil, redness, or pus leaking from around my bottom.
I have felt minor stinging once or twice in the past with hard stools, but nothing anywhere near this excruciating.
No, I haven't felt dizzy, lightheaded, or like I might faint.
No, my weight has been stable and I haven't felt unusually tired.
No heartburn, acid regurgitation, nausea, or vomiting of blood.
No, I haven't eaten beets, blueberries, dark gelatin, or blood sausage.
I have struggled with chronic constipation for several years, but I have no other chronic medical conditions.
No, I have never had surgery or been hospitalized for anything.
I am not currently taking any prescription medications or over-the-counter supplements.
No, I do not take aspirin, ibuprofen, blood thinners, or iron supplements.
No, I do not have any known allergies to medicines.
No, I have never had hepatitis, cirrhosis, or any liver problems.
I drink one or two beers on the weekend with friends, nothing heavy.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I work as an office clerk sitting at a desk all day, and I live with my partner.
No, I have never had a colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy done.
My father has high blood pressure, but no one in my family has had colon cancer, polyps, or inflammatory bowel disease.
I was wondering if I might have developed severe hemorrhoids.
I am terrified to use the bathroom because the pain is so unbearable every time I have to go.
I was really hoping you could prescribe a numbing cream or ointment to help relieve the pain.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Standing blood pressure 118/76 mmHg and heart rate 78 beats/min, showing no orthostatic hypotension or tachycardia.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are clear and anicteric.
Abdomen is flat and symmetrical with no surgical scars, distension, or visible pulsations.
Normoactive bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants; no abdominal bruits.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended across all quadrants with no palpable mass or organomegaly.
Visual inspection of the perianal area reveals a superficial longitudinal mucosal tear in the posterior midline, without external hemorrhoids, skin tags, or purulent drainage.
Severe anal tenderness and marked sphincter spasm upon attempted finger insertion; examination is deferred due to excruciating pain.
